metadata.title: ICCS 2016 National Report Malta 2016
metadata.venue: IEA (International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This ICCS 2016 Malta national report describes the ICCS international study design for Year 9 students (approximately age 14) and reports descriptive statistics and regression analyses using scale scores derived from IRT (Rasch partial credit) and a civic knowledge achievement scale. The report states that participation rates were required at the school and student levels (e.g., 85% of selected schools and 85% of selected students, or a weighted overall participation rate of 75%), but it does not specify the application of student/sampling weights in the analysis results presented here. No replicate-weight methodology (e.g., BRR/jackknife) or explicit weight variable names are reported. Because the manuscript does not document whether complex survey weights were applied to the reported means/percentages/regression coefficients, weighting is treated as not reported for the purposes of this extraction.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The report does not use ICCS achievement plausible values (PV) in the sense of PISA/TIMSS PV methodology; instead, it reports an ICCS civic knowledge achievement scale derived from the Rasch model and questionnaire scale indices standardized to a mean of 50 and SD of 10. Missing data handling is not described (no imputation/deletion protocol is reported), representing a methodological reporting gap for any inferential modeling beyond the descriptive summaries. The dependent variables are scale scores and regression outcomes based on Rasch-scaled constructs rather than PV-based cognitive achievement scores.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Analytic sample comprises the Maltese Year 9 cohort assessed in ICCS 2016: all students in intact classrooms within the selected 47 secondary schools in Malta and Gozo. The report states that the Maltese student group included 3,764 students (953 males, 998 females in State/Church/Independent school categories) and that the cognitive test was administered using a balanced rotated design (eight booklets; each student completed one booklet in 45 minutes). No additional exclusion criteria (e.g., missing questionnaire/test completion rules) are explicitly documented in the provided text; therefore, the analytic sample is treated as the full available Year 9 cohort for Malta as described.

data.outcome_summary: This ICCS 2016 Malta national report analyzes Year 9 civic knowledge attainment (ICCS civic knowledge scale) and related constructs derived from Rasch scaling of questionnaire items. The report does not apply machine learning; instead, it uses descriptive comparisons and multiple regression models linking civic knowledge to sets of predictors. For engagement predictors, the regression explains 28.2% of the variation in ICCS scores, with most engagement traits significant (except willingness to participate in school activities). For value beliefs and attitudes, the regression explains 34.9% of the variation, with gender equality attitudes as the strongest significant predictor and country-of-residence attitudes not significant. For European perspective predictors, the regression explains 32.3% of the variation, with attitudes toward restricting worker migration the strongest significant predictor; European identity and equal-rights-for-immigrants attitudes are not significant. Methodologically, the report does not document plausible-value handling or missing-data handling, and it does not specify whether complex survey weights were applied.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction targets an official assessment framework, user guide, or technical manual without an empirical ML study. Sample sizes, ML algorithms, and predictive findings are intentionally null or empty per schema rules for non-empirical IEA/OECD documentation.
